clue.text: Concede when worth toilet training

indicators.note: training something reshapes it, so these three words are reshaped into a new order of letters

explanation.surface: A parent gives up on potty-training a stubborn toddler, wondering whether it is worth the effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'training' is the anagram signal: the fifteen letters of WHEN, WORTH and TOILET are rearranged into the four-word phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom from boxing, where a trainer tosses a towel into the ring to surrender for a beaten fighter.

clue.text: Author not available to support small firm over summons

indicators.note: in a down clue a piece that supports another sits beneath it, so the author and NA go below
in a down clue, over means the word for a small firm is turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: bus. is a short form of business, a firm
Edgar Allan Poe, the American writer

explanation.surface: A writer short of work helps out a little company, but is served with legal papers.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'over' turns BUS upside down to SUB, and 'to support' puts POE + NA underneath it.
explanation.definitionFit: A writ ordering someone to attend court is a formal legal summons.

clue.text: It is so evident in one famously very old

indicators.note: evident in says the answer can be seen inside the name the next words point to, the rest of that name falling away

parts.note: Methuselah, the Biblical patriarch said to have lived 969 years

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that great age is plain to see in a famously ancient figure.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits not in the clue's own words but inside METHUSELAH, which 'one famously very old' points to: 'evident in' strips ME and ELAH from either side.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means in this way, and the phrase it is so asserts exactly that manner or truth.

clue.text: Lure fish to island on the fringes of Malaysia

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it, so the island letters come before the fringe letters

parts.note: the char is a trout-like freshwater fish

indicators.note: the fringes of a word are its outermost letters, its first and last

explanation.surface: An angler tries to tempt fish towards an island off the coast of Malaysia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the fringes of' takes M and A, the outer letters of Malaysia.
explanation.definitionFit: Personal magnetism is an allure that draws people, so the noun lure fits as a synonym.

clue.text: Organism takes a short time first emerging by artifice

parts.note: mo is short for moment, a brief time

indicators.note: first here asks for the opening letter of each of the three following words

explanation.surface: A creature is said to come into being quickly through some trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' takes E, B and A, the initials of 'emerging by artifice'; 'takes' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A single-celled protozoan is a simple living thing, an example of an organism.

clue.text: Scoot off with photograph of vision in darkness

indicators.note: off here means gone wrong or awry, so the letters of the first word are jumbled

parts.note: pic is an informal word for a photograph

explanation.surface: Someone runs off clutching a snapshot taken at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges SCOOT into SCOTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Scientific adjective for the rod-based eyesight humans use in dim light, the opposite of photopic.

clue.text: Strength required for first managing cryptic clues

indicators.note: first asks for the opening letter of the word that follows it
cryptic means puzzling or obscure, so the letters of the next word are scrambled

explanation.surface: Solving cryptic clues demands real mental power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' takes M from managing; 'cryptic' rearranges CLUES into USCLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Physical power or clout, as in political muscle, is a synonym for strength.

clue.text: Computer essential for hospital activity to get statutory covering support

parts.note: operating is what surgeons do in a hospital theatre

indicators.note: the covering of a word is its outer shell, its first and last letters

parts.note: a stem supports a flower or leaf

explanation.surface: Hospital IT staff need legal backing for their computer work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' takes S and Y, the outer letters of statutory, placed before STEM.
explanation.definitionFit: The core software such as Windows or Linux is something no computer can run without.

clue.text: Swift horse you resolved to enter in very hard inaugural National Hunt November meeting

indicators.note: to enter in means the scrambled letters go inside the two letters for very hard

parts.note: HH is the pencil grading for very hard lead

indicators.note: resolved means worked out afresh, so the three letters of you are rearranged
inaugural means opening, so the first letter of each following word is taken

explanation.surface: A fast racehorse is entered for the first National Hunt race meeting in November, on very firm going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swift' is the author Jonathan Swift, not speed. HH is the pencil grade for very hard, and National Hunt is British jump racing over fences.
explanation.definitionFit: In Gulliver's Travels by Jonathan Swift, the rational horses ruling their land are called by this name.

clue.text: Friend finishing up a complete fool

parts.note: a chum is a close friend

indicators.note: finishing points to the final letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A friend ends up looking a complete idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finishing' takes P, the last letter of up.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British insult for a foolish person, a synonym of idiot.

clue.text: Adversary in military manoeuvre has a tricky problem

parts.note: op is short for a military operation
a poser is a puzzling question

explanation.surface: An enemy in a military exercise sets a difficult puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who stands against you is an opponent, a synonym of adversary.

clue.text: Nectarine not an unusual tempter

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary, so the remaining letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rare nectarine proves especially tempting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not an' removes A and N from NECTARINE, and 'unusual' rearranges the leftover ECTRINE.
explanation.definitionFit: One who lures or tempts others is a synonym for a tempter.

clue.text: Detailed perfect scheme

indicators.note: read as de-tailed, the word that follows loses its tail, its final letter

parts.note: ideal means perfect

explanation.surface: A meticulously worked-out plan is described as flawless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detailed' is read as de-tailed: IDEAL loses its last letter L.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan or notion one has in mind is a synonym for a scheme.

clue.text: Recent maps show this landscape feature

indicators.note: show is used loosely as display in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Up-to-date maps mark a feature of the terrain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'show' rearranges RECENT MAPS.
explanation.definitionFit: A long steep slope or cliff face at the edge of a plateau is a feature of terrain.

clue.text: Internal airline reportedly to keep in touch with receiver

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the following words are said aloud for their sound

parts.note: to track something is to follow it and stay in touch with it; the ear receives sound

explanation.surface: An internal air service promises to keep contact with someone taking the call.
explanation.walkthrough: TRACK plus EAR, said aloud, gives the sound of the answer. 'airline' is not a carrier but a pipe for air.
explanation.definitionFit: The windpipe carries air inside the body, a whimsical airline within the chest.

clue.text: Pig farmer gets extremely angry at the end of the year

parts.note: a hog is a pig
a man who keeps pigs; together the first two words read as pig man

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of the next word, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A pig farmer gets very cross as the year closes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pig farmer' gives HOG MAN, a pig man; 'extremely' takes A and Y from angry. The answer is the Scottish New Year's Eve celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: Scottish name for the festivities of 31 December, when the old year closes.

clue.text: Sale with a changed drawing power

indicators.note: changed means one letter is swapped for another, here the a named in the clue

parts.note: an auction is a sale by bidding

explanation.surface: A sale that has been altered gains pulling power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with a changed' swaps the A of AUCTION for S.
explanation.definitionFit: Suction is the force that pulls air or fluid in, so drawing power describes it.

clue.text: Sterilise hospital shortly before it is stripped clean

parts.note: san is short for sanatorium, a kind of hospital

indicators.note: stripped means the outer letters are taken away, leaving the middle of the next word

explanation.surface: A hospital rushes to disinfect, then is scrubbed clean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stripped' leaves E, the middle of clean. 'shortly' trims sanatorium to SAN.
explanation.definitionFit: To make free of germs is to disinfect, a synonym of sterilise.

clue.text: Firmly fixed that setter is to be tucked up for the night

parts.note: the setter speaks as I, so setter is gives I'm
bedded means put to bed

explanation.surface: The puzzle-maker insists on being tucked up in bed for the night.
explanation.definitionFit: Embedded, set deep and secure in surrounding material, is a firm fixing.

clue.text: Ring for this appointment?

definitions.meaning: a ring is given to mark a betrothal
a booked meeting or date in a diary

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether they should telephone to book a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like a phone call to make an appointment, but it is the ring a fiancée receives.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a betrothal sealed with a ring, and a booked appointment in a diary.

clue.text: A verdict on mulligatawny soup, given without lawman being present

indicators.note: soup suggests a mixed-up mess, so the leftover letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A court rules on a curry soup served without the police being present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without lawman' removes L, A, W, M, A, N from MULLIGATAWNY, and 'soup' stirs the remaining ULIGTY. Mulligatawny is a spiced Anglo-Indian soup.
explanation.definitionFit: Juries return a finding of culpable or not; this is one of the two possible outcomes.

clue.text: Poster writer

definitions.meaning: one who posts something, sending it by mail

explanation.walkthrough: 'Poster' looks like a wall bill, but it means one who posts letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: someone who sends things by mail, and the American novelist Norman Mailer.

clue.text: Bird found mostly in the same place

indicators.note: mostly means nearly all of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: the word in, given as written before trimming
bis is a musical direction to repeat a passage, going back to the same place

explanation.surface: A bird is usually seen at the same spot.
explanation.walkthrough: The blog reads 'mostly in the same place' as IBID less D, which leaves the final S unexplained; I from 'in' cut short plus BIS, the repeat sign, accounts for every letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-billed wading bird, sacred in ancient Egypt, is one kind of bird.

clue.text: Reformed paper not the middle state school one

indicators.note: the middle asks for the central letter of the preceding word

parts.note: RI is the abbreviation for Rhode Island, a US state
a gam is a school of whales
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A newspaper reformed itself to stop backing middle schools and state schools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the middle' takes O from not.
explanation.definitionFit: The Japanese art of folding paper into shapes gives sheets a new form.

clue.text: Harangues one involved in deals

indicators.note: involved in means the letter for one goes inside the word for deals

parts.note: trades are deals
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: Someone launches into rants about business deals.
explanation.definitionFit: Long angry speeches are rants, the noun sense of harangues.

clue.text: Argues over part of the make-up of crosswords

definitions.text: part of the make-up of crosswords
definitions.meaning: the horizontal lines of squares in a grid; plural, as the grid has many

explanation.surface: Solvers bicker about how crossword grids are built.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: noisy quarrels, verb form, and the horizontal lines of squares forming a grid.

clue.text: Counts as a run outside

definitions.meaning: in cricket, a bye or wide is a run not scored off the bat
the Latin prefix in words like extramural means outside

explanation.surface: A cricket scorer notes that a stray run counts.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, runs from byes, wides and no-balls are not credited to the batsman but still count to the team's total.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a cricket run not off the bat, and the Latin prefix meaning beyond or outside.

clue.text: South African golfer's clothing reportedly lacking presence

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is heard, so the words are said aloud for their sound

parts.note: Ernie Els, the South African golfer; wear is clothing, as in menswear

explanation.surface: A South African golfer's outfit, by all accounts, lacks impact.
explanation.walkthrough: ELS plus WEAR, said aloud, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in some other place means not being here, so absent, lacking presence.
